articleBody:
Before signing a contract for new kitchen surfaces, reviewing the fine print protects your project schedule and budget. Use this checklist to confirm every detail is accounted for before work begins.

- [ ] Cabinet level verification — A run exceeding 1/8 inch out of level can crack rigid stone slabs or create unsightly gaps beneath the surface.
- [ ] Physical sink and cooktop presence — Installers require actual fixtures or exact cutout templates on site before fabricating holes.
- [ ] Seam placement agreement — Marking exact seam locations on layout drawings prevents visible cuts across primary prep zones.
- [ ] Overhang support brackets — Stone overhangs extending past roughly 6 to 8 inches require steel plates or corbels fixed to cabinets.
- [ ] Edge profile selection — Specifying eased, bullnose, or beveled edges up front prevents costly change orders during CNC cutting.
- [ ] Plumbing disconnection responsibilities — Clarifying whether the contractor or a licensed plumber handles sink and faucet shutoffs avoids day-of delays.
- [ ] Existing countertop tear-out plan — Documenting whether removal and disposal of old tile, laminate, or stone tops are included in the scope.
- [ ] Fabrication lead-time estimate — Confirming the 1 to 3 week fabrication turnaround window keeps cabinet and appliance crews on schedule.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through these items with your general contractor or countertop installer during the initial consultation.
